title: How Often Should You Review Your Insurance? The Annual and Milestone Rule
description: Discover when and how often to review your insurance coverage: the annual policy audit rhythm and the 7 life milestone triggers that demand immediate policy updates.
author: Marcus Vance

content.text: Insurance is not a 'set-it-and-forget-it' financial product. As your life progresses, your assets grow, your liabilities change, and construction inflation erodes your dwelling coverage. Failing to review policies regularly is the primary cause of catastrophic [underinsurance](/learn/how-to-know-if-you-are-underinsured).

items: The Annual Policy Review: Conduct a 30-minute audit once per year (ideally 30 days before your homeowner or auto policy renewal date).
Milestone-Triggered Reviews: Review your portfolio immediately upon experiencing any of the 7 major life transitions below.

content.text: The 7 Life Milestones That Trigger a Policy Review

rows: Getting Married / Divorced
Combine auto policies for multi-car discount; update life insurance beneficiaries.
Proceeds going to an ex-spouse or missing out on bundling discounts.
Welcoming a Baby / Adopting
Increase term life coverage multiple; add newborn to health plan within 30 days.
Losing health coverage special enrollment window or underinsuring child support.
Home Renovation / Addition
Increase dwelling limit (Coverage A) on homeowner policy by remodel cost.
Co-insurance penalties if home burns down after a $100k kitchen remodel.
Adding a Teenage Driver
Add teen to auto policy; raise liability limits and explore good-student discounts.
Denied claims or catastrophic multi-million dollar liability lawsuits.
Starting a Home-Based Business
Add a home business endorsement; personal home insurance excludes commercial loss.
Zero coverage if business inventory is stolen or a client slips on your steps.
Significant Pay Raise / Asset Growth
Add an Umbrella Liability policy ($1M - $5M) to protect growing net worth.
Lawsuit judgments seizing non-exempt investment and brokerage accounts.
Paying Off Your Mortgage
Contact insurer to remove the bank as loss payee and verify continuing coverage.
Inadvertent policy lapse if escrow payments cease.

content.title: Guidance from the Insurance Information Institute
content.text: The [Insurance Information Institute (III)](https://www.iii.org/) recommends using annual open enrollment periods to re-verify employer disability, life, and health plan coverage caps.

content.title: Audit Your Current Coverage Gap
content.description: Review whether your existing policies match your current family and debt obligations.

items.question: How long do I have to add a newborn baby to health insurance?
items.answer: Most health plans provide a strict 30-day Special Enrollment Period following birth or adoption. If you miss this 30-day window, your baby cannot be added until the next annual open enrollment.

content.text: Policy review guidelines are educational. Consult your licensed insurance agent to execute policy updates.
